proposals.evidence: DEDR5151 gives Irula dāru who, Kota ār/dār and Kannada ār/dāru. LSI āru Who? fits this interrogative family, preserving its lack of initial d and final u; the proposed parent is the whole article family.

proposals.evidence: DEDR5151 includes Tamil eṉṉa what and ēṉ/eṉ/eṉai why/what, Kannada ēn what and Kodagu ennï what. LSI Irula yenna appears in both What? and Why? slots; propose the interrogative family for both while preserving initial y, doubled n and the two distinct source meanings. This does not assert identical morphology for all cited comparanda.

proposals.evidence: DEDR333 explicitly gives Tamil ām yes (from ākum), Malayalam ām assent and Kannada āṃ assent in the be/become family. LSI Irula āma Yes is proposed in that affirmative family, retaining final a. The article also compares Indo-Aryan forms, but that comparison does not identify an immediate donor or require a borrowing link here.
